mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns do not exceed the baseline mean when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative equity returns as consumer and business confidence declines.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive when UNRATE increases by >0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in housing starts and retail sales indicates a slowdown in aggregate demand, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive when both HOUST and RSAFS show weakness.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth reflects strong economic activity, which is positive for corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity markets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns do not exceed the baseline mean when PAYEMS grows.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL increases by >2pp.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate alongside increasing unemployment indicates monetary tightening, negatively impacting equity markets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive when FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both increase.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in federal funds rate may signal tighter monetary policy, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5pp.
